name: General Mitchell International Airport
before:
Milwaukee's airport, 9 km south of downtown, and a genuinely easy one to use. It serves southern and eastern Wisconsin and northern Illinois, which makes it a real alternative to Chicago for clients heading to that corner of the Midwest.

One terminal, two concourses, 38 gates. Southwest and United are in Concourse C and everyone else in Concourse D. International arrivals without border pre-clearance go through the separate International Arrivals Building.

It has more character than most American airports. There is an aviation museum and a USO room on the concession level, children's play areas throughout, and a branch of Renaissance Books which is believed to be the world's first second hand bookshop in an airport. An observation area on the north edge is open to the public, with tower radio traffic rebroadcast on low power FM so visitors can listen in the car.

The airport is named after General Billy Mitchell, who grew up in Milwaukee and is often called the father of the United States Air Force.
after:
Milwaukee's airport, 9 km south of downtown, serving south-eastern Wisconsin.

One terminal with two concourses, C and D. Southwest and United use Concourse C, while American, Delta and Alaska use Concourse D. International arrivals, apart from flights from Toronto, go through the separate International Arrivals Terminal north of the parking structure.

The main terminal has the Mitchell Gallery of Flight, a free aviation museum before security, next to a USO lounge for military personnel. There are children's play areas throughout and a branch of Renaissance Books, which sells second-hand and rare books.

The airport is named after General Billy Mitchell, who grew up in Milwaukee and is often called the father of the United States Air Force.
